assumptions: K=2 frozen learned candidates and U in {1,5} are declared before data.
Collection groups are mutually independent and exchangeable after conditioning on every frozen artifact.
Both exact success floors assume zero harmful groups.
Every group is opportunity-bearing for the joint best-case floor.
The tail floor uses the maximally favorable cap-to-zero sample and is a non-vacuity floor, not statistical power for a practical effect.
The latency cap is an estimand-defining engineering bound, not a parameter to choose after inspecting outcomes.
The measured COMMECT campaign remains one group and is never reinterpreted as admission evidence.

formulas.joint_best_case_group_floor: max(n_min, success_zero_harm_group_floor, tail_best_case_group_floor) when every group bears an opportunity
formulas.tail_best_case_group_floor: smallest G whose production bounded-CVaR gain LCB reaches delta for reactive=latency_cap and candidate=0
formulas.zero_harm_success_group_floor: ceil(log(alpha_endpoint)/log(1-epsilon)), adjusted to the smallest integer satisfying 1-alpha_endpoint^(1/G)<=epsilon

measured_reference.reason: COMMECT is one continuous drive, so every requested n_min is at least five times the available opportunity-bearing independent-group count.

warning: Prospective design sensitivity only: do not choose a gate configuration after inspecting policy-selection or test outcomes. If configurations are outcome-selected, they must be added to the protected multiplicity family before data are observed.
